A managed policy rather than a first-run preferences seed, for two reasons.
It applies to EVERY profile on the machine, which matters here because each
web app in the dock runs with its own --user-data-dir and a seeded default
would have to be copied into each one. And it survives a profile reset,
so 'clear browsing data' does not quietly put DuckDuckGo back.
Debian's Chromium ships DuckDuckGo as the default. Nothing wrong with it,
but on this machine the search box should reach the same index the rest of
the OS searches - teddyos-search and the address bar answering from two
different corpora is the kind of split that makes a system feel assembled
DefaultSearchProviderEnabled is deliberately NOT paired with a policy that
removes the others: the provider list stays editable, so this is a default
and not a lock-in. Someone who wants Google should get it in two clicks.
